## Verification-then-close: alarm condition cleared; the defect lives in aa7b-5e47

Re-checked the LIVE state before closing, as the handoff comment required (not closed on the handoff alone):

- The underlying defect — outbound comment sync not idempotent, comment_ids dedup map never populated — was extracted to bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615), which is now **closed**. This ticket's own comments record the recovery: root cause fixed, cleanup across 33 issues verified against backups, bridge re-enabled, `comment_ids` 0 -> 303, outbound posts 251 -> 14 -> 1, five consecutive green runs.
- Live re-check (2026-08-21 ~17:30Z, `gh run list --workflow=reconcile-bridge.yml`): the two most recent scheduled runs succeeded (32498339191 @ 15:34Z, 32503636020 @ 16:34Z). Latest success is ~1h old, so the canary condition (no success within 4h) does NOT currently hold.
- NEW, separate observation recorded for the operator: three runs earlier today (32482642367 @ 12:35Z, 32487786991 @ 13:37Z, 32492914442 @ 14:34Z) failed with a DIFFERENT mechanism — reconcile completed (`BRIDGE_STATE: converged`, all batch_outcome error=None) but the final push of the tickets branch was rejected `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`. That is a push race on the tickets ref, NOT the duplication defect this canary tracked. Per the handoff's own instruction, a fresh alarm is a new finding deserving its own investigation, not an append here — noting it so it is not lost; it has since self-cleared (two green runs after).

Closing: this canary fired correctly, its firing condition no longer holds, and the defect it surfaced is fixed and closed in aa7b-5e47.
